leads.usedFor: Found HB 78, the Consumer Data Privacy Act bill
Bill status: passed House Oct. 1, 2025; Senate second consideration June 25, 2026; not enacted

consumer_health_data.note: Keyword searches of the session laws returned no results for these terms. HB 78, a consumer data privacy bill, passed the House in 2025. Its last action was Senate second consideration on June 25, 2026. It is not law.

crossCheck.note: Both official statute searches return nothing for consumer health data. HB 78 page shows last action Senate second consideration on June 25, 2026. Not enacted. No in-force provision found.

feeRules: 42 Pa.C.S. 6155(b)(1): patient fee may not exceed the amounts in 6152(a)(2)(i).

42 Pa.C.S. 6152(a)(2)(i) base amounts: "$20.62 for searching for and retrieving the records, $1.39 per page for the first 20 pages, $1.03 per page for pages 21 through 60 and 34¢ per page for pages 61 and thereafter", adjusted yearly by CPI.
42 Pa.C.S. 6152.1(a)(1): "a flat fee of $19" plus postage for records supporting a Social Security or needs-based benefit claim or appeal, adjusted yearly.
55 Pa.B. 8441 (effective Jan. 1, 2026): pages 1-20 $2, pages 21-60 $1.48, pages 61 on $0.52, microfilm $2.95, search and retrieval $29.61 not chargeable for own record, benefit-claim flat fee $37.52.
28 Pa. Code 115.29 (hospitals): charges "shall be reasonably related to the cost of making the copy".

provisions.title: Rights of patients: rights to records generally
provisions.quote: A health care provider or facility shall not charge a patient or his designee, including his attorney, a fee in excess of the amounts set forth in section 6152(a)(2)(i) (relating to subpoena of records).

provisions.title: Subpoena of records: fee amounts
provisions.quote: The payment shall be $20.62 for searching for and retrieving the records, $1.39 per page for the first 20 pages, $1.03 per page for pages 21 through 60 and 34¢ per page for pages 61 and thereafter for paper copies or reproductions on electronic media
provisions.appliesTo: "the health care provider or facility or a designated agent"

provisions.title: Limit on charges for benefit claims
provisions.quote: a health care provider or facility shall not charge more than a flat fee of $19 for the expense of reproducing medical charts or records, plus the actual cost of postage, shipping or delivery
provisions.appliesTo: Requests "for the purpose of supporting a claim or appeal under any provision of the Social Security Act" or a needs-based benefit program

provisions.title: Department of Health notice: Amendments to Charges for Medical Records
provisions.quote: Search and retrieval of records (cannot be charged if requestor is requesting their own personal health record)
provisions.appliesTo: "a health care facility or health care provider"

provisions.title: Hospital regulation: patient access
provisions.quote: The patient or the patient’s next of kin may be charged for the cost of reproducing the copies; however, the charges shall be reasonably related to the cost of making the copy.
provisions.appliesTo: Hospitals licensed under the Health Care Facilities Act

leads.usedFor: Pointed to the yearly Pa. Bulletin fee notice

copy_rights.note: No state deadline under 30 days and no free copy case found. The state sets per-page caps and a $19 base flat fee for benefit claims, not a free copy. Caps do not count. Not beyond the federal floor.

crossCheck.note: beyondFederalFloor: no. No deadline under 30 days in 42 Pa.C.S. 6155 or 28 Pa. Code 103.22 and 115.29. The benefit-claim rule caps a fee, it is not free. Per-page caps never count.

hie_consent.designatedHie: Pennsylvania Patient & Provider Network (P3N), run by the Department of Human Services eHealth Partnership Program

provisions.title: Human Services Code, consent and confidentiality of health information: opt-out registry
provisions.citation: Human Services Code (Act of June 13, 1967, P.L.31, No.21) § 1407-C(c)(1), added by Act 76 of 2016
provisions.quote: In order to decline participation in the health information exchange, a patient must sign and date a form declining participation.
provisions.appliesTo: The Statewide health information exchange established under Article XIV-C

provisions.title: Human Services Code: published consent form and notice
provisions.quote: The department shall publish a consent form including notice of a patient's ability to decline to allow exchange of the patient's electronic health information in the health information exchange.

leads.usedFor: DHS page confirming P3N under Act 76 and a published patient opt-out form

hie_consent.note: Records are exchanged unless the patient signs an opt-out form. DHS publishes the form. Section 1407-C(a)(2) keeps other laws needing added consent. Whether HIV records need consent for P3N exchange was not resolved.

crossCheck.note: Section 1407-C added by Act 76 of 2016, effective immediately on July 8, 2016. DHS publishes the opt-out form. stricterForSensitive stays unresolved; HIV Act 7(a)(6) lets providers in the person's care receive HIV data.

provisions.title: Abortion Control Act: reporting, confidentiality of reports
provisions.quote: shall remain confidential, except that disclosure may be made to law enforcement officials upon an order of a court of common pleas after application showing good cause therefor.
provisions.appliesTo: Reports filed with the Department of Health under subsections (a) and (h)

leads.usedFor: Checked for a shield law on reproductive health data; none listed

reproductive.note: The rule covers abortion reports filed with the Department of Health. Disclosure to law enforcement needs a court order. No statute on reproductive data sent to other states was found. Subsection (e) was last amended by Act 31 of 1988.

crossCheck.note: Covers abortion reports filed with the Department of Health. Act 31 of 1988 amended subsection (e), effective 30 days after March 25, 1988. Shield bills from 2025 are not enacted.

provisions.title: Mental Health Procedures Act: confidentiality of records
provisions.citation: Mental Health Procedures Act § 111(a) (Act 143 of 1976; 50 P.S. § 7111)
provisions.quote: All documents concerning persons in treatment shall be kept confidential and, without the person's written consent, may not be released or their contents disclosed to anyone except:
provisions.appliesTo: Documents concerning persons in treatment under the act

mental_health.note: Act 32 of 2022 added an exception for HIPAA covered entities and business associates acting under 45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E. Privileged communications still need written consent.

crossCheck.note: Section 111(a) last amended by Act 32 of 2022, which took effect immediately on July 7, 2022. The act page confirms this.

provisions.title: Confidentiality of HIV-Related Information Act: confidentiality of records
provisions.quote: No person or employee, or agent of such person, who obtains confidential HIV-related information in the course of providing any health or social service or pursuant to a release of confidential HIV-related information under subsection (c) may disclose or be compelled to disclose the information
provisions.appliesTo: Any person who obtains confidential HIV-related information while providing a health or social service

hiv.note: Disclosure is limited to listed persons or a written consent meeting section 7(c). Section 8 limits court orders for access.

crossCheck.note: Act of Nov. 29, 1990, No. 148, effective in 90 days. The 2011 amendments by Act 59 touched sections 2, 5 and 6, not section 7.

leads.usedFor: Genetic privacy bill HB 1530; bill only

genetic.note: Search results showed DNA database, paternity testing, genetic counselor licensing and insurance references to federal GINA. No state rule on confidentiality of genetic test records was found.

crossCheck.note: Searches for genetic information and genetic test hit DNA databases, vital statistics, paternity and GINA references only. HB 1530 sits in a Senate committee since Dec. 22, 2025. Not enacted.

facts.statutoryDamages: None. Compensatory damages; attorney fees and costs for section 6 violations by a source patient's physician.

provisions.title: Confidentiality of HIV-Related Information Act: civil cause of action
provisions.quote: Any person aggrieved by a violation of this act shall have a cause of action against the person who committed such violation and may recover compensatory damages.
provisions.appliesTo: Violations of the HIV-Related Information Act

provisions.title: Breach of Personal Information Notification Act: civil relief
provisions.quote: The Office of Attorney General shall have exclusive authority to bring an action under the Unfair Trade Practices and Consumer Protection Law for a violation of this act.
provisions.appliesTo: Violations of the breach notification act

private_right.note: The only right to sue found covers HIV-related information, one narrow category. The breach act gives the Attorney General exclusive enforcement. No general right to sue over medical records was found.

crossCheck.note: Right to sue covers HIV-related information only. The breach act leaves enforcement to the Attorney General. No statutory damages; attorney fees only for section 6 violations by a source patient's physician.

provisions.title: Breach of Personal Information Notification Act: definition of personal information
provisions.citation: Act 94 of 2005, § 2 (73 P.S. § 2302), as amended by Act 33 of 2024
provisions.quote: (iv) Medical information in the possession of a State agency or State agency contractor. (v) Health insurance information.
provisions.appliesTo: "An entity that maintains, stores or manages computerized data that includes personal information"

provisions.title: Notice to Attorney General
provisions.quote: When notice of the breach of the security of the system under this section must be given to more than 500 affected individuals in this Commonwealth, notice shall be made concurrently to the Office of Attorney General.
provisions.appliesTo: Breaches affecting more than 500 Pennsylvania residents; entities under 40 Pa.C.S. Ch. 45 are exempt

provisions.title: Notice timing
provisions.quote: Except as provided in section 4 or in order to take any measures necessary to determine the scope of the breach and to restore the reasonable integrity of the data system, the notice shall be made without unreasonable delay.
provisions.appliesTo: Entities holding computerized personal information of Pennsylvania residents

provisions.title: Entities subject to HIPAA
provisions.quote: Any covered entity or business associate that is subject to and in compliance with the privacy and security standards for the protection of electronic personal health information established under the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996
provisions.appliesTo: HIPAA covered entities and business associates

leads.usedFor: AG page confirming Sept. 26, 2024 effective date of amendments

breach_health.note: Both elements are in the definition. Medical information counts only when held by a State agency or State agency contractor. Health insurance information has no such limit. Medical information added by Act 151 of 2022.

crossCheck.note: Definition amended by Act 33, approved June 28, 2024, effective Sept. 26, 2024. Medical information counts only for State agencies and contractors. Notice without unreasonable delay. AG notice over 500. HIPAA-compliant entities deemed compliant.
